title: add: JSONSchema response_format with strict-mode validation and clearer error messages
author: Aisha Patel
release_notes: Add response_format JSONSchema support with a strict mode that enforces exact validation of model outputs; improved validation error messages returned to callers and updated OpenAI-compat layer to translate legacy response_format shapes.
description: Adds first-class JSONSchema support to the response_format parameter across the Redwood API and OpenAI compatibility layer. Motivation: customers want strong structured output guarantees for downstream parsers and safety checks. This PR introduces a 'json_schema' response_format implementation and a configurable 'strict' validation mode. In strict mode the runtime validates the model output against the provided JSON Schema and returns a clear structured error when validation fails; in non-strict mode the runtime attempts to coerce/parsing-fallback and still returns the model output with validation diagnostics. The change touches API surface, compatibility translation, runtime validation utilities, streaming stabilization to include partial validation hints, unit/integration tests, and docs/examples. Key behaviors: 1) New response_format shape accepted by both native Redwood API and OpenAI-compatible endpoint. 2) 'strict: true' causes a ValidationError response with code 'response_format.validation_failed' and a structured message listing failing paths, expected schema snippets, and original model text. 3) Streaming behavior: when schema validation is enabled, the streaming channel will emit a preliminary validation-metadata event if partial tokens can already be validated; final validation result is emitted as a trailing event. 4) Backwards-compatible fallthrough: old clients that do not pass response_format continue to get legacy text responses. 5) Extensive tests and docs added, and migration notes for customers using OpenAI-compat wrappers.

review_thread: Evan Brooks (reviewer) on 2026-02-11: High-level LGTM. Please ensure validation errors are compact and machine-parseable. Also add e2e fixture for an intentionally malformed schema.
Aisha Patel (author) on 2026-02-11: Thanks Evan — added machine-friendly ValidationError payload and a new e2e fixture (tests/integration/test_response_format_jsonschema.py).
Lina Morales (reviewer) on 2026-02-12: Question: will strict mode cause hard 4xx responses? We should document retry semantics for clients.

Aisha Patel on 2026-02-12: Strict mode surfaces a 400-like validation error with code 'response_format.validation_failed'. We added docs and migration note describing recommended client behavior (retry with relaxed mode or fix prompt/schema).

Samuel Grant (reviewer) on 2026-02-13: Minor nit: streaming metadata event introduces an extra SSE message type. Make sure the OpenAI-compat layer maps it to a 'delta' chunk that clients can ignore if not recognized.
Aisha Patel on 2026-02-13: Updated compat translator to emit a compat delta and documented it in the examples.

testing_notes: Added unit tests for validator edge cases, integration e2e that runs model stub to simulate invalid JSON, and an end-to-end compatibility test that verifies OpenAI-compat translation.
docs_note: docs/api/response_format.md documents new response_format JSONSchema shape, examples for strict and non-strict modes, and migration guidance for OpenAI-compat clients.
observability_changes: Added validation.metrics.schema_validation_failures with tags: repo, endpoint, strict_mode; tracing span 'jsonschema.validate' added to generation trace.
performance_considerations: Validator runs incrementally and uses cached compiled schemas; worst-case overhead measured at ~2-5ms per request for typical schemas. We added a circuit-breaker to skip expensive validation for very large schemas if CPU quota is constrained.
migration_guidance: OpenAI-compat: response_format objects with legacy shapes will be translated. Clients that want strict validation should set 'response_format': {"type": "json_schema", "schema": <schema>, "strict": true}. See docs for examples.
